chapter: Willie Cornish: war service and personal history
title: Willie's portrait and his Spanish-American War discharge papers
summary: Bella shows the framed portrait and the war honor roll; the interviewers read his company, regiment and enlistment date of July 22, 1898.

blocks.x: Oh, no, he got me. I have his picture in here, where I had his picture, you know, in the bedroom.
Oh, can I help you with that?

Yeah, this is his picture. This cost me $14. A man down there fixed this for me. That's all I had. So that's a great big one. That wasn't taken. Was that taken from here? Yes, sir. He took five of them. Then he sent me a letter, and he told me to come, and I went down there, and he kept one, way down on Roy Street. Now, and I picked that. And then he fixed that frame that made it show up, and everybody says it's like him.
Well, this gives all about his company. That's nice. Did you want to read that out? Yeah.
Everybody says it's like him.
Let me read this. It says, Role of Honor, World's Great War for Freedom.
I know I would find it.
World's Great War for Freedom. United we stand. It looks like it has an American flag and an English flag.
The Spanish American flag. Oh, that's the Spanish flag. The Spanish American flag is yellow. See, I know.
It says, W.M. Cornish. Company F. Regiment 9th U.S. VOL. I guess that's Volunteer.
Volunteer.
Infantry INF.

Yeah. Yeah. It's a reason that the man didn't write it all on there like he should have. I had it on another piece of paper somewhere. Let me see. Somewhere else I had it. The man didn't fix it correctly. He fixed it like that. I said, well, Benzie, fix it like that. I'm going to carry it home. I ain't going to say no more to the man because he might mess it up.
That's right.
Yeah, some of them mess it up. That's the picture I showed you. Isn't it? Yeah.
Mm-hmm. That's right.
Yeah, that's the picture I showed him. Huh?
That's the other one. It's the one I saw.
That's the picture I showed him.
Yeah, that's the same picture though.
And then you've seen the picture of the other consigned too where the man down in St. Bernard. That's the one. I'd give anything to get that.
It says, uh, place of enlistment NOLA. New Orleans, Louisiana.
Mm-hmm.
Date of enlistment July 22nd, 1898. Camp Corbin, Louisiana.
See, this is what I took to get the money off him. Oh my God, I like to woe out.
Oh, that's...
That's what I took to get the money off him. I woe out. The man woe me out going there. He woe me out. And I wrote that down myself, you know. Yeah.
Yeah.
Yeah.
It says served two years. Mm-hmm. You better read all this in case some of this might be different because I've checked that.
The man didn't fix it right on there like he should have. Like I told him. He didn't fix it all on there. Because the man figured... He got paid for it, but he didn't fix it. You understand?
Is this an XC-2-3-7-3-1-3-1? Yeah. That was a long one. Mm-hmm. Might be XG-2-3-7-3. What do you mean this year?
Yeah. Oh no, that's a XG. And that's a 2 and that's a 3-7-3-1-3-1.
